item.text: {"search_note":"I found no 2024 evidence that Kishida used emergency powers, security laws, surveillance, or administrative controls to create a broader political fear climate. The available record is much stronger on reassurance, child protection, disaster resilience, and rights language than on coercive domestic control.","evidence":[{"title":"Video Message by Prime Minister Kishida at the Symposium on Inclusive Society and Human Rights","publisher":"Prime Minister’s Office of Japan","date":"February 5, 2024","url":"https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202402/05_message.html","summary":"Kishida said people in Japan should not be subjected to discriminatory treatment or violence, explicitly said the government would stand firm against prejudice, and framed “human dignity” and “safety and security” as the goal. This is a hard-security measure, but the source presents it as expert-led and legal, not as intimidation or mass surveillance.","question_ids":["3B.6","3B.5","3B.4"]}]}
